decisions.rationale: Simulator side reproduced. The query in the finding (instructors unaliased, a second copy AS manager) gives 'ERROR: invalid reference to FROM-clause entry for table "instructors"', and SQLCHK.explain adds 'use the alias, not the table name'. The server side has not been run. It comes from the cited SELECT/alias documentation (an alias hides the name only of the FROM item it is written on), and I agree with that reading. The root cause is resolve() in the sql-practice@1 adapter (authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/engine.js), which this branch must not edit, and the ERROR line itself, presented as PostgreSQL wording, cannot be corrected in scope. This is serious for a page that teaches the alias rule, so it needs a tooling decision: an adapter version that fixes resolve() and is confirmed on a server. Rule I apply to every adapter-fidelity defect in this module: escalate when the false Output itself cannot be made honest in scope; accept, with an in-loop mitigation plus a recipe finding, when page-owned bytes can stop the defect from misleading the learner. Mitigation the author should still make in this loop, in controller.js: when the failing statement names the same table twice and only one copy has an alias, explain says 'this practice editor needs an alias on each copy of a table joined to itself' (do not state server behaviour in learner text, since nobody has run it), and keeps the current sentence for the genuine case. Keep the Activity 3 two-alias requirement as a lesson rule, worded as such.

Verified. The Activity 3 editor alt in src/anti-joins-and-self-joins.body.html, which artifact.md copies under Static interaction alternatives, says 'on employee.lead_id = manager.instructor_id', and so does the topic.js sql[3].fallback ('from employee.lead_id to manager.instructor_id'). The same condition is also the keyed retry answer. Fix every surface: alt, fallback, static exercise text, artifact.md, the Activity 3 checks and hints (see C2E-ANTI-01) and the sql[3] near-miss note ('joining employee.lead_id to manager.instructor_id'). Describe the relationship (lead_id stores the instructor_id of that instructor's lead) instead of the ON expression, and keep the expected-output description. The recap cheat sheet row 'employee.lead_id = manager.instructor_id' may stay, because engine.css hides the recap (.recap.is-pending, display: none) until every activity is settled.

Reproduced. With an unqualified 'WHERE course_id IS NULL' the result is exactly Femi, but the check unsets the rows tick and says 'find it with a LEFT JOIN to enrollments and an IS NULL test on that right-side key', which contradicts a query that does exactly that. The check requires x.a.qual===alias in src/anti-joins-and-self-joins.topic.js. Acceptable fix: accept an unqualified student_id or course_id in the IS NULL test when the column exists only in enrollments (course_id), or when the reference resolves to the enrollments item. This loosens what completes the activity, but it is a correctness check on the query, not the attempt, retry or credit rules that the captain decision covers. If the task owner reads 'grading' as covering check criteria, use the critic's wording-only fallback: keep the criterion and make the note ask for the qualified form explicitly ('qualify it with the enrollments alias, for example e.course_id'). Either way the note must stop calling a correct LEFT JOIN ... IS NULL query wrong.

Verified the GIFT text: the 'o2 self-join condition' distractor's feedback says 'so each occurrence needs its own alias'. The server behaviour is unexecuted, but from the cited alias documentation only distinct reference names are needed, and the same quiz's 'why two aliases' item already says 'each appearance needs its own name'. Fix the feedback wording in artifact.gift, with wording that is true however the server rule is read, for example 'the two copies of employees need different names; give each copy a role alias such as e and m'.

Verified. The Activity 3 checks say 'joined from the employee's lead_id to the manager's instructor_id', hint 2 says 'Compare the employee's lead_id with the manager's instructor_id', and the task supplies the aliases, column names and sort. The direction is the one reasoning step, and it is also the Activity 4 retry answer. Fix: word the check by result ('Each instructor's row shows the name of the instructor their lead_id points at'), make hint 2 a reasoning step (which row stores the link, which row it points at), and remove the direction from every other surface listed under C2S-ANTI-02. Severity note: the reading column's worked example (w.lead_id = l.instructor_id) already shows the shape, as C1 requires, so critical may be one step high. The fix stands.

Verified. Activity 4's teaching describes NOT EXISTS (SELECT ...) and i.instructor_id in prose only. The first complete NOT EXISTS forms appear in the options, with SELECT 1 unexplained, 'courses c' written without AS (the page writes AS everywhere else), and the outer FROM instructors AS i never shown. The courses rows behind 'Course 104 has a NULL instructor_id' are not visible in Activity 4 (C1, C2). Fix: add one complete worked NOT EXISTS query with its outer FROM and result, on a different pair from the question (for example courses with no enrollment), explain SELECT 1 in a clause, show the courses rows (course_id, instructor_id) the question relies on, and write AS in the options. Update topic.js why/miss text where it names the alias.

Verified. Every unreadable statement, the empty-file prompt and every real subset limit reach the shell as kind 'limit' from the adapter's check() in authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/engine.js; I reproduced 'SELEC * FROM students;', a missing comma between two VALUES rows, a missing semicolon before a second SELECT and the untouched starter, all kind 'limit'. authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/controller.js relabels 'limit' as 'Not in this practice editor', and LIMITS item 4 in authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/build.mjs plus every page's Sources footer ('not as invalid PostgreSQL') say that label never means the SQL is wrong. The label is page-owned, so it is fixable in scope. Acceptable fix: in controller.js, wrap EDITOR.check (EDITOR is Object.create of the adapter) and re-kind problems by message into three classes. Real subset limits (WITH, psql meta-commands, CREATE TABLE and so on) keep 'Not in this practice editor'. Unreadable statements ('could not read the statement near', 'could not read one starting') get a learner label such as 'Check your SQL'. The empty-file prompt gets its own neutral label. Message matching is feasible: I checked that real limits carry their own messages ('WITH queries are outside this practice editor', 'CREATE is not available here', 'Transactions are outside this practice editor', 'COPY runs on the database server', and the psql meta-command text), distinct from the unreadable-statement messages. Never use the adapter's own 'Lesson check' (B4), and never use kind 'hint', because the shell blocks Run only on non-hint problems. Run gating, the 'limit' notRun status and onSqlRun's 'did not use up a try' path must stay exactly as they are (E2 is pending). Reword LIMITS item 4 and the footer sentence in each src/<topic>.body.html and artifact.md to match. The minimum acceptable fix, if message matching seems too brittle, is one neutral label covering both cases, with LIMITS and footer sentences that no longer say the SQL is fine. Shell wording stays a recipe finding.

Verified in the page simulator. A missing semicolon at the end of line 3 is reported at Ln 4 near "select", and a missing comma at the end of line 2 of a multi-row VALUES is reported at Ln 3 near "(" (policy 1.3, E5). Where the location comes from (the adapter's Limit token line in authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/engine.js) is out of scope, so record a recipe finding: the adapter should report the end of the previous token. In-loop fix, per policy 1.3's second bullet: in the same controller.js check wrapper, when the message is 'could not read the statement near' and the token is first on its line, either point Ln at the previous non-blank line or append 'If this line looks right, check the end of the line before it for a missing comma or semicolon.' Wording and location only; run gating does not change.

Reproduced. An unqualified name in the Activity 3 self-join gives 'column reference "name" is ambiguous', and SQLCHK.explain in authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/controller.js hard-codes 'for example s.name'. No alias s exists, and following the suggestion gives 'missing FROM-clause entry for table "s"' (reproduced on the joins page). Fix in controller.js: take the example alias from the failing statement's own FROM/JOIN items (o.st.from[].alias, falling back to the table name), or, if none is available, say 'the alias you gave that table'. This one change also fixes C2E-JOIN-01 and C2S-JOIN-02.

Verified. Activity 2 hint 1 says 'Copy the shape of the courses example: students on the left, enrollments on the right, joined on student_id', and hint 2 says 'Test the enrollments alias's student_id with IS NULL'. Together they dictate the statement and repeat the teaching (D5). The sql[2] notes also say 'tests the enrollments alias's student_id with IS NULL'. Fix: make hint 2 a reasoning step ('Which column can only be NULL when no enrollment matched?'), keep hint 1 to the left/right decision without spelling out the clause, and word the matching topic.js notes the same way.

Verified. The task uses aliases employee and manager and also output columns employee and manager, while the inner-and-left-joins page defined an alias as 'a short nickname' (courses AS c) and this page's example uses w and l. Low-cost fix: add one clause that an alias can be any name, even a whole word, or use distinct alias names. Verified. The 'o2 self-join condition' options write bare JOIN, and the module always writes INNER JOIN; no page says JOIN alone means INNER JOIN (searched all eight artifact.html files). Fix: write INNER JOIN in the four options of artifact.gift, or add the equivalence to inner-and-left-joins teaching. Changing the GIFT is the smaller change.

Verified strings. The authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/build.mjs badge reads 'Practice editor: follows PostgreSQL on this page's sample tables' and the status span reads 'SQL practice editor'. In authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/controller.js, EDITOR.language='PostgreSQL server' feeds the shell's Output header '(lesson simulator, not real PostgreSQL server)', while SQLCHK.explain says 'PostgreSQL cannot tell which one you mean' / 'PostgreSQL would stop with the ERROR'. The shell's empty Problems text is 'No problems found by the lesson checker', which also uses B4 grader vocabulary. C2 F5 says a page never says both 'not real' and 'PostgreSQL rejected'. In-loop fix, page-owned bytes only: use one name ('practice editor') in the build.mjs badge and status span, choose EDITOR.language so the shell header reads consistently with it, and word the explain lines as what 'a real PostgreSQL server' would report. The shell's 'lesson simulator, not real' prefix and its 'No problems found by the lesson checker' sentence are engine.js shell bytes: record a recipe finding.

Verified. CONF in authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/build.mjs prints Low / Medium / High, but DESIGN.md (Assessment: options, confidence, feedback) sets "Guessing", "Fairly sure", "Certain". In authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/controller.js, checkPredict writes 'Your guess was not this time', and summarize() joins open activities as 'Activity '+open.join(' and '), which gives 'Activity 2 and 3 and 4 are'. Fix, wording only: in CONF, use the DESIGN.md labels (the radio values low/medium/high may stay). calibration() echoes the raw value ('Your confidence: medium'), so map it to the shown label. Write 'Your guess was not right this time', and join a list as 'Activities 2, 3 and 4 are' (singular 'Activity 2 is').

Reproduced at 570x1000 under file:// and over http://127.0.0.1: scrollY 157, exactly the top of #activity-1. At 1280 px it is 121 on inner-and-left-joins and 0 where the document fits. Cause confirmed: with history.replaceState stubbed out, scrollY stays 0. The last line of authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/controller.js calls go(...,'replace'), whose history.replaceState(#activity-1) runs during parsing. It does not throw, and the browser's load-time scroll-to-fragment then scrolls to #activity-1, so F1 fails on the narrow frame (G7). Fix in controller.js: on first load with no #activity-N in the URL, do not write a hash (call go with no history mode), or write it after load and keep scroll at 0. Keep the hash behaviour for later navigation. Measured in headless Chromium only; check the platform embed after the fix.
